plasmid pAMI 2 of P. aminophilus contains a three-gene operon that is crucial for methylotropic growth on DMF, that the operon is regulated by a LuxR family regulator, and that the genes of the operon are involved in the biotransformation of DMF.
plasmid pAMI 2 of Paracoccu s aminophilus carries a three-gen e cluster coding for the N,N-dimethy lformamide degrada tion-related genes whose expression is activated by a LuxR fami ly regulator.

the plasmid pAMI1 of the bacterium Paracoccus aaminophilus JCM7686, which is involved in the degradation of the toxic solvent N,N-dimethyformamide (DMFA), carries a three-genes cluster coding for DmfR, a positive transcription regulator of the LuxR protein family, and two subunit (DmfA and DmfA) of an N,N-dimetyformamidase that is crucial for DMF degradation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification, genetic characterization, and expression of the genes responsible for the degradation of DM F by P. aminophilus, a microorganism which is able to grow on DMF as the only carbon source.
the characterization of plasmid pAMI1 of Paracoccus sp. strain JCM 7688.
the identification of the genetic basis of methylotrophic growth on DMF by P. aminophilus and the construction of a strain able to grow on DMF at a high concentration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has provided new insights into the genetic basis of the biodegradation of DMF, a toxic industrial chemical.
the genes of pAMI2 constitute the first known genetic determinants of DMF degradation in bacteria.

this study provides the first insights into the genetic basis of DMF degradation in bacteria and that the results obtained may contribute to the development of biotechnological applications for the biodegradation of this toxic solvent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasmid pAMI1 from Paracoccus aminiophilus carries the genes for the degradation of N,N-dimetilformamide, which are regulated by the positive regulator DmfR.
the plasmid pAMI-2 carries a DMF degradation-related gene cluster whose expression is activated by a LuxR family regulator.
the genetic information of pAMI2, a plasmid of Paracoccus sp. JCM 7685, is crucial for methyltrophic growth on DMF as the only carbon source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LuxR-type regulator DmfR is responsible for activating the transcription of a methylotrophic DMF degradation pathway.
the genes involved in the catabolism of DMF are clustered in an operon whose transcription is regulated in a LuxR family-dependent manner.

the plasmid pAMI 2, which is widespread among methylotrophic Paracoccus strains isolated in Japan and other countries, carries a three-gon cluster coding for the N,N-dimetylfornamide (DMF) degradation enzymes DmfA1, DmfA2, and DmfR, whose expression is activated by the positive transcriptional regulator DmfR in the presence of this toxic solvent.
